audit.whatIsWrong: His ultimate is written as 'Noxus Guillotine' in five places across the content layer — spikes[1].text, wants.you[1], wants.foe[1], the mid text and whys[4]. The real name is Noxian Guillotine. Crippling Strike (W) is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's R is Noxian Guillotine: 'Darius leaps to an enemy champion and strikes a lethal blow, dealing true damage. This damage is increased for each stack of Hemorrhage on the target. If Noxian Guillotine is a killing blow, its cooldown is refreshed.' The refresh-on-kill is the part that matters and the page never says it. Crippling Strike is a 5s attack reset that slows — against a champion whose entire plan is kiting at Twin Fang range, an attack reset that removes her move speed is the ability that actually converts his pull into a kill, and it is the wind-up you read, not the cast.
audit.corrected: Name corrected to Noxian Guillotine everywhere, its kill-refresh added, and Crippling Strike's 5s reset-and-slow named in the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is called the clock this lane runs on in eight places and its cooldown appears nowhere.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s — the longest cooldown either champion has in the early game, and it is 26 seconds at rank 1. That single number changes the advice from 'bait it, count it' into something a player can actually act on: a whiffed pull is not a moment, it is most of a wave. Noxian Guillotine is 120/100/80s but refreshes on a kill.
audit.corrected: 26s at rank 1 and 16s maxed added to the win condition, cooldown block, do's, early text, mid text, all-in windows and key interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicts its own whys at four stages, and diff reads HARD while diffRating says 4/10 and breakdown.difficulty says 'Favoured matchup'.
audit.why: whys[2] says his all-in peaks at 3 and 'beats your two-ability poke', whys[3] calls 4-5 'his strongest window', whys[4] says 'Genuinely even at 6', whys[5] says 'Roughly even' at first item. So Level 3 and Levels 4-5 are Darius's and Level 6 and First item are Skill — which is exactly the level chart carried in the source packet, so the current win array has drifted away from both the packet and the prose.
audit.corrected: win[2]=Darius, win[3]=Darius, win[4]=Skill, win[5]=Skill, phase sides matched, diff set to EVEN to agree with its own 4/10.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are a knife-edge — Darius wins the raw all-in but you have the poison engine. Do NOT walk into his E (Apprehend) range to last-hit; he pulls you, lands the Q (Decimate) outer blade to heal and damage, and stacks Hemorrhage bleed that out-trades your single ability at level 1. Last-hit with the tail of Q (Noxious Blast) from max range, and the moment you hit 2-3 with Q and E you can prime poison and chain a Twin Fang or two when he steps up to farm — chip him, then back off on your Q move-speed buff before he closes.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are a knife-edge — Darius wins the raw all-in but you have the poison engine. Do NOT walk into his E (Apprehend) range to last-hit; he pulls you, lands the Q (Decimate) outer blade to heal and damage, and stacks Hemorrhage bleed that out-trades your single ability at level 1. Apprehend is 26s at rank 1, so a whiffed pull hands you a genuinely long window. Last-hit with the tail of Q (Noxious Blast) from max range, and once you hit 2-3 you can prime poison and chain a Twin Fang or two when he steps up — chip him, then back off on your Q move-speed buff.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his peak and your hardest stretch — every rank makes his empowered Q hit harder and his bleed all-in more lethal, and you still cannot win a straight melee exchange. Save W (Miasma) exclusively for his E (Apprehend) pull or his walk-up: grounding cancels the gap-close and lets you back-pedal on your passive (Serpentine Grace) speed while Q-E poison ticks. At 6 it equalizes — your R (Petrifying Gaze) stuns his all-in attempt and answers a dive, but his R (Noxus Guillotine) true-damage execute means if you are ever low you still die through the kite, so never fight him below that missing-HP threshold.

notes: DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE — needs a ruling. Six strings say Miasma's grounding 'cancels his only gap-close' / 'grounds his E pull' (wants.you[0], spikes[2], spikes[3], the mid and late text, whys[6]). Riot's Apprehend text is 'Darius sweeps up his enemies with his axe's hook and pulls them to him' — that is a displacement applied to Cassiopeia, not movement by Darius, so grounding him plausibly does nothing to stop it. The ability of his that IS his own movement is Noxian Guillotine, which 'leaps to an enemy champion'. Whether grounding blocks either is exactly the class of thing the kit files mark as unknown, so I did not rewrite or delete any of it. If grounding does not stop Apprehend, six strings are teaching players to hold a 24s cooldown for a moment it cannot save them, and that is the highest-value single fix left on this page. Also: Apprehend carries a knockup flag in the kit; Riot's text says only that he pulls enemies to him, so I never described it as a knockup.
